problems.problem:
The figure shows the insulin signal transduction pathway in simplified form. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-1-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Glukose = glucose; Insulin = insulin; Insulin-Rezeptor = insulin receptor; Glykogen = glycogen; Pyruvat = pyruvate; Fettsäuren = fatty acids.

A. The insulin receptor is activated by the uptake of glucose into the cell.

B. Signal transduction from the insulin receptor inhibits glycogen synthesis.

C. The imported glucose can be metabolised to pyruvate.

D. Pyruvate can be assembled into fatty acids.

The figure shows a bacterial cell schematically. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-2-fig1.png

A. Structure A is called the nucleus.

B. The structure of B differs between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

C. C serves for protein synthesis.

D. Structure D is a flagellum.

Certain enzymes can be activated by phosphorylation. This means that a phosphate group ($\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}$) is attached to the enzyme. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Phosphorylations are irreversible modifications.

B. Phosphorylation can cause a conformational change (change of the 3D structure).

C. In addition to the phosphate, a positively charged group must be attached.

D. Phosphorylations are catalysed by kinases.

In which metabolic pathway is oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) consumed directly?

A. Lactic acid fermentation

B. Glycolysis

C. Citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle)

D. Oxidative phosphorylation

In the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, toxic substances are detoxified and lipids are synthesised, among other things. Indicate for each of the following cell types whether you would expect it to have a particularly large smooth ER (true) or not (false).

A. Testosterone-producing Leydig cell

B. Antibody-producing plasma cell

C. Epidermal cell

D. Liver cell

The following molecules and complexes are ordered by their mass. Which is the correct order?

A. Amylase > ribosome > $\mathrm{CO_2}$ > glucose

B. Glucose > amylase > ribosome > $\mathrm{CO_2}$

C. Ribosome > glucose > amylase > $\mathrm{CO_2}$

D. Ribosome > amylase > glucose > $\mathrm{CO_2}$

There are different types of cell–cell communication. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. For a cell to be able to respond to a hormone signal, it needs the corresponding receptors.

B. Communication via nerve signals is faster than hormone signalling.

C. Hormones can only act extracellularly.

D. Hormone signalling is suitable for bringing about long-term adaptation.

Light striking the eye triggers the reaction shown in the figure. So that further light signals can be received, retinal is brought back into its original form by an enzyme. What type of reaction is the reaction catalysed by light and the enzyme?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-8-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Retinal = retinal; Licht = light; Enzym = enzyme.

A. An isomerisation

B. A reduction

C. A condensation

D. An elimination

Enzymes accelerate chemical reactions in all living organisms. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The 3D structure of enzymes changes when the substrate is bound.

B. Enzymes are used up in every reaction.

C. The activity of enzymes depends on the temperature.

D. Enzymes shift the equilibrium towards the products.

A yeast cell produces a fluorescent membrane protein. In which order do the cell organelles light up?

(A) Golgi apparatus (B) plasma membrane (C) vesicle (D) endoplasmic reticulum

A. A → C → D → C → B

B. D → B → C → A → B

C. D → C → A → C → B

D. C → D → B → A → B

In cancer, uncontrolled cell divisions take place. Indicate for each of the following approaches whether it is a possible therapy (true) or not (false).

A. Preventing the formation of the mitotic spindle

B. Overexpressing receptors for growth signals

C. Preventing DNA replication

D. Preventing the formation of new blood vessels

Freeze fracturing is an important technique for studying membranes. In it, a cell is frozen in liquid nitrogen and its membrane is then broken open (see figure). The membranes can then be viewed under the electron microscope. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-12-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): äussere Schicht = outer layer; Messer = knife; Zelle = cell; Eisblock = ice block; Protein = protein; innere Schicht = inner layer.

A. Transmembrane proteins prevent two lipid layers from separating.

B. The movement of transmembrane proteins in the plasma membrane can be observed directly with this method.

C. Protein complexes in membranes can be viewed with this method.

D. The freeze-fracture technique can show that membranes consist of a bilayer.

Indicate for each of the following elements whether it is taken up by land plants mainly through the stomata (true) or not (false).

A. Carbon

B. Nitrogen

C. Phosphorus

D. Hydrogen

The figure shows photosynthesis in CAM (crassulacean acid metabolism) plants schematically. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-14-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Nacht = night; Tag = day; Stärke = starch; Triosephosphat = triose phosphate; Pyruvat = pyruvate; Apfelsäure = malic acid.

A. Molecule a is oxygen.

B. Organelle 2 is a mitochondrion.

C. At the end of the night, the pH in the vacuole (organelle 1) is lower than in the evening.

D. Metabolic pathway I is glycolysis.

Aphids (Aphioidea) secrete a sticky, sugary liquid when they infest a tree. Which plant structure is therefore tapped by the aphids?

A. Pith

B. Phloem

C. Resin duct

D. Xylem

The figure shows the alternation of generations of ferns (Pteridophyta) schematically. In the sporangium, haploid spores are formed by meiotic division. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-16-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Sporophyt = sporophyte; Sporangium = sporangium; Spore = spore; keimende Spore = germinating spore; Gametophyt = gametophyte; männliche Keimzelle = male gamete; männliches Geschlechtsorgan = male sex organ; Eizelle = egg cell; weibliches Geschlechtsorgan = female sex organ; neuer Sporophyt = new sporophyte.

A. Fertilisation takes place during A.

B. The sporophyte is haploid.

C. There are separate female and male plants.

D. The diploid stages of ferns are unicellular.

The figure shows the structure of a plant organ schematically. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-17-fig1.png

A. C serves for gas exchange.

B. Structure A is called the cuticle.

C. B consists mainly of photosynthetically active cells.

D. The figure shows the structure of a root.

Look at the diagram of a plant cell and indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-18-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Plasmamembran = plasma membrane; glattes ER = smooth ER; rauhes ER = rough ER; Mitochondrium = mitochondrion; Zellkern = nucleus; Kernhülle = nuclear envelope; Lysosom = lysosome; Kernpore = nuclear pore; Golgi = Golgi; freie Ribosomen = free ribosomes; Peroxisom = peroxisome.

A. Structure A consists mainly of proteins.

B. Photosynthesis takes place in structure B.

C. Mainly water-soluble substances are stored in structure C.

D. Structure D is called a stoma.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it applies to mosses (Bryophyta) (true) or not (false).

A. Mosses have cell walls.

B. Mosses transport water through the xylem.

C. Mosses carry out photosynthesis.

D. Mosses can reproduce sexually.

The figure shows schematically the signals that trigger germination in tobacco seeds (Nicotiana) (GA = gibberellic acid, ABA = abscisic acid, BR = brassinosteroids). Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-20-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): intakter Samen = intact seed; Samenschale = seed coat; Endosperm = endosperm; Keimblätter = cotyledons; Licht = light; Samenschale durchbrochen = seed coat ruptured; Endosperm durchbrochen = endosperm ruptured; Ethylen = ethylene; gekeimter Samen = germinated seed; Hemmung = inhibition; Aktivierung = activation.

A. Ethylene inhibits germination.

B. Light triggers the production of gibberellic acid.

C. Abscisic acid inhibits germination.

D. Gibberellic acid enhances the effect of abscisic acid.

To investigate the effect of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) on elongation growth, shoots were treated with IAA and sugar (see figure). Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-21-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Verlängerung (% ursprünglichen Länge) = elongation (% of original length); Zeit (h) = time (h); IAA + Zucker = IAA + sugar; Zucker = sugar; pH in der Zellwand = pH in the cell wall; Länge = length; Verlängerung (µm) = elongation (µm); Zeit nach IAA (min) = time after IAA (min).

A. After 10 minutes, IAA has developed its full effect on elongation growth.

B. IAA causes acidification of the cell wall.

C. The effect of IAA and sugar corresponds to the sum of the effects of sugar and IAA alone.

D. IAA can only bring about cell elongation if sugar is added.

In paraplegia, the spinal cord is completely or partially severed. The patients can no longer move their legs voluntarily. Often, however, the reflexes in the legs still work. Why is this so?

A. The neurons involved are connected locally in the spinal cord (reflex arc).

B. The neurons involved are more robust than motor neurons.

C. The neurons involved can grow back together after a spinal cord injury (regeneration).

D. The neurons involved run to the brain via the abdominal cavity (ventral nervous system).

Most neurons communicate via chemical synapses. In this process, the presynaptic cell releases a neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft. This neurotransmitter then binds to a receptor in the postsynaptic membrane and triggers a signal there. How can the activity of the postsynapse be increased? Indicate for each of the following measures whether it does this (true) or not (false).

A. Releasing more neurotransmitter

B. Inserting more receptors into the postsynaptic membrane

C. Widening the synaptic cleft

D. Inhibiting neurotransmitter-degrading enzymes

Which of the following graphics correctly depicts a human retina (Retina)?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-24-fig1.png

For which of the following substances does the concentration in the exhaled air of land mammals differ, in percentage terms, most from that in the inhaled air?

A. Carbon dioxide

B. Argon

C. Nitrogen

D. Carbon monoxide

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Bile helps in the digestion of fats.

B. Bile is produced by the liver.

C. Bile is stored in the liver.

D. Bile is amphiphilic (fat- and water-soluble).

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Adrenaline is an antagonist of glucagon.

B. Adrenaline inhibits digestive activity.

C. Adrenaline stimulates the sympathetic nervous system.

D. Adrenaline is secreted by the pituitary gland.

In a congenital heart defect, the wall between the atria is not completely closed. Which changes can thereby be observed in an affected newborn compared with a healthy one? Indicate for each of the following suggestions whether it applies (true) or not (false).

A. The $\mathrm{N_2}$ concentration in the pulmonary vessels is increased.

B. The thickness of the left ventricular wall is reduced.

C. The oxygen saturation measured on the finger is increased.

D. $\mathrm{CO_2}$-rich blood can pass from the right into the left atrium.

An animal bone gets stuck in the trachea of a Persian leopard (Panthera pardus ciscaucasica). Which changes can be detected in the blood in the first minutes afterwards? Indicate for each of the following suggestions whether it is true or false.

A. Rise in nitrogen

B. Fall in oxygen

C. Rise in adrenaline

D. Fall in lactate

Involution is defined as the natural regression of an organ that is active only for a limited time. Indicate for each of the following examples whether this structure undergoes involution (true) or not (false).

A. Mammary gland at the end of the lactation period

B. Lymph node at the end of an inflammatory reaction

C. Lung at the end of a marathon

D. Uterus at the end of pregnancy

During development, in most male mammals the so-called descensus testis (descent of the testes) takes place. Why is this important?

A. The testes are better protected in this way.

B. The blood supply of the testes is better ensured in this way.

C. The testes no longer have room behind the kidneys.

D. The sperm cannot tolerate the high body temperature.

The contraceptive pill contains oestrogens and progestogens. The figure shows schematically the hormonal control circuit of female sex hormones. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it applies to a woman taking the contraceptive pill (true) or not (false).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-32-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Follikelreifung = follicle maturation; Östrogen = oestrogen; Corpus luteum = corpus luteum; Eisprung = ovulation; Gestagene = progestogens; Gebärmutterschleimhaut = uterine lining; Hemmung = inhibition; Aktivierung = activation.

A. The release of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is inhibited.

B. The uterine lining is no longer built up.

C. Follicles mature nevertheless.

D. Ovulation is prevented.

Indicate for each of the following processes whether it is important for successful embryogenesis (true) or not (false).

A. Cell communication

B. Cell migration

C. Cell differentiation

D. programmed cell death (apoptosis)

Osteoclasts are cells that break down mineralised bone by acidifying the environment. The figure shows an osteoclast. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-34-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Osteoklast = osteoclast; Mineralisierter Knochen = mineralised bone; © Institut für Anatomie, Universität Bern = © Institute of Anatomy, University of Bern.

A. The osteoclast pumps protons into the extracellular space.

B. The osteoclast takes up the breakdown products.

C. The osteoclast has a small surface-area-to-volume ratio.

D. The osteoclast has a high metabolic rate.

Which function(s) does the acidic environment of the stomach fulfil in digestion? Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The acid cleaves the peptide bonds in proteins.

B. The acid kills acid-sensitive bacteria.

C. The acid neutralises the basic saliva in the chyme.

D. The acid creates an ideal environment for certain digestive enzymes.

A patient complains of pain in the knee joint and can hardly move it any more. The treating doctor suspects an inflammation. Indicate for each of the following findings whether it supports the doctor's hypothesis (true) or not (false).

A. An increased level of white blood cells (leukocytes)

B. An increased level of red blood cells (erythrocytes)

C. Reduced blood flow

D. Increased permeability of the blood vessels

In an experiment, it was tested by which features young gulls recognise their parents. For this, various dummies were held up to them and it was measured how often the chicks responded to these dummies by pecking. The results are shown in the figure. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is correct (true) or not (false).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-37-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Anwesenheit vom Fleck auf Schnabel = presence of the spot on the beak; Schnabelform = beak shape; Kontrolle = control; Picken (% relativ zur Kontrolle) = pecking (% relative to control); Kopfform = head shape; Kopffarbe = head colour; nur Schnabel = beak only.

A. The gulls recognise their parents more by the beak than by the head.

B. The spot on the beak is clearly more important than a realistic head shape.

C. A realistic head colour is clearly more important than a realistic head shape.

D. The thick beak is preferred over the thin beak.

Müllerian mimicry occurs when two or more well-defended (e.g. poisonous) species develop a similar warning coloration and their predator thus develops an aversion to them more quickly. Indicate for each of the following cases whether it is Müllerian mimicry (true) or not (false).

A. A non-poisonous butterfly shows the same pattern as a poisonous one.

B. A stick insect looks like a leaf.

C. A cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) and a leopard (Panthera pardus) have a similar coat pattern.

D. Two poisonous wasp species are striped black and yellow.

Indicate for each of the following behaviours whether it is innate (true) or not (false).

A. The feeding of cheeping chicks by bird parents

B. The burying of nuts in autumn by squirrels

C. The ability of a parrot to utter certain words

D. A dog sitting down at the command "Sit"

How does genetic variation arise?

A. Isolation

B. Mutation

C. Migration

D. Selection

Indicate for each of the following traits whether it is inherited according to Mendel's rules (true) or not (false).

A. Point mutation in the CFTR gene on chromosome 7

B. Mutation in the mitochondrial DNA

C. Ampicillin resistance in bacteria

D. Body weight

Through massive use of antibiotics in hospitals and in agriculture, more and more antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains are arising. Why? Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Resistance genes shorten the generation time.

B. Antibiotics directly increase the mutation rate.

C. The widespread use of antibiotics causes frequent bottleneck effects.

D. The selection pressure of the antibiotics increases the fitness of the resistant bacteria.

In a test cross, an individual is crossed with a partner that is homozygous for the recessive allele. Indicate for each of the following statements about test crosses whether it is true or false.

A. If the tested individual is heterozygous, all offspring show the dominant phenotype.

B. If the tested individual is homozygous, the offspring show a ratio of 3:1.

C. From the phenotypes of the offspring, conclusions can be drawn about the genotype of the individual.

D. The results of a test cross can be explained with Mendel's model.

Adaptive radiation is the diversification of a little-specialised species into many specialised ones (e.g. Darwin's finches). Indicate for each of the following suggestions whether adaptive radiation can be caused by it (true) or not (false).

A. Unoccupied ecological niches

B. Acquisition of a new trait that allows the colonisation of new habitats

C. Radical change of the environment

D. Genetic drift

Complex traits are influenced both by the genome and by the environment. To investigate the extent of the two influences, twin studies can be carried out. In these, the agreement of traits (concordance) between twins is determined. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false for a trait with a very strong genetic influence. (Note: siblings means full siblings who are not twins.)

A. The concordance is much greater in identical twins separated after birth than in those not separated.

B. The concordance is greater in identical twins than in fraternal twins.

C. The concordance in siblings is about the same as in step-siblings.

D. The concordance is smaller in fraternal twins than in siblings.

Look at the pedigree in the figure and indicate for each of the following suggestions whether the trait grey fur could be inherited according to this mode of inheritance (true) or not (false).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-46-fig1.png

A. X-linked recessive

B. Autosomal dominant

C. X-linked dominant

D. Autosomal recessive

You cross a white Labrador with a brown one. They have 10 puppies: 5 white, 3 black, 2 brown. (B: black, b: brown, A: coloured, a: white). Allele A (coloured) must be present for the phenotypes black (B) or brown (b) to appear at all. What is the genotype of the parents?

A. Aabb × aaBb

B. aabb × aaBb

C. Aabb × aabb

D. Aabb × aaBB

Indicate for each of the following statements about inbreeding whether it is true or false. Inbreeding …

A. … can be used to increase the frequency of a desired trait.

B. … leads to sterile offspring.

C. … increases the proportion of homozygotes.

D. … increases the mutation rate during cell division.

In Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$. $p$ and $q$ are the allele frequencies. $2pq$ corresponds to …

A. … the proportion of homozygotes in the parental generation.

B. … the proportion of heterozygotes in the population.

C. … the number of dominant individuals in the daughter generation.

D. … the number of zygotes of the first generation.

Which of these definitions best describes the concept of fitness in evolution?

A. Fitness measures how much an individual contributes to the gene pool of the next generations.

B. Fitness describes the individual health and strength of an individual.

C. Fitness is a measure of the ability of an organism to adapt to its current environment.

D. Fitness indicates how many sexual partners each individual in the population can choose.

Most leopards (Panthera) are spotted, but there are also melanistic (black) individuals, especially at high altitudes and in the rainforest. The black coloration of the fur is inherited autosomally recessively via a single gene. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. There are more black females than black males.

B. A black leopard will have black offspring regardless of the coat colour of its partner.

C. Two spotted leopards can have a black cub.

D. If the spotted sister of a black leopard has offspring with the spotted brother of a black leopard, 50% of the offspring will be black.

An analogy (= derived trait) is a trait that has arisen independently in species that are not closely related, as an adaptation to similar environmental influences. Indicate for each of the following pairs of traits whether it is an analogy (true) or not (false).

A. Stinging cells (cnidocytes) of jellyfish and corals

B. Jumping legs of kangaroos and Patagonian maras

C. Four-leggedness in dogs and frogs

D. Wings of bats and birds

The biospecies concept defines a species as a "group of natural populations that can interbreed with one another and are reproductively isolated from other groups". Indicate for each of the following situations whether the biospecies concept is sufficient to distinguish species from one another (true) or not (false).

A. Donkey and horse, which together can produce sterile offspring (mule/hinny)

B. Fossils

C. Closely related species that mate at different times

D. Asexually reproducing organisms

The Persian leopard (Panthera pardus ciscaucasica) belongs to the Panthera lineage. The figure shows the phylogenetic tree of the cat family (Felidae). Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-54-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Hauskatzenartige = domestic cat lineage; Leopardenartige = leopard cat lineage; Pumaartige = puma lineage; Luchsartige = lynx lineage; Ozelotartige = ocelot lineage; Wüstenluchsartige = caracal lineage (literally "desert-lynx-like cats"); Pantherartige = Panthera lineage; Kleinkatzen = small cats; Grosskatzen = big cats; gemeinsamer Vorfahr = common ancestor.

A. The Persian leopard belongs to the outgroup.

B. A living member of the lynx lineage is evolutionarily younger than a living puma.

C. The Panthera lineage forms a monophyletic group with the caracal lineage.

D. The leopard cat lineage is more closely related to the common ancestor than the domestic cat lineage.

Diclofenac is a lipophilic molecule that is used as an anti-inflammatory drug both in veterinary and in human medicine. Cow carcasses contaminated with diclofenac led to a massive die-off of vultures. It was striking that whole flocks of vultures died at once. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Cows can break down diclofenac only poorly.

B. Vultures often feed as a flock on the same carcass.

C. To save the vultures completely, the use of diclofenac in humans would also have to be banned.

D. Diclofenac remains in the fatty tissue of the cows.

Indicate for each of the following climate zones whether you would expect particularly many plants with felty leaves in it (true) or not (false).

A. Tropical zone

B. Subtropical zone

C. Temperate zone

D. Alpine zone

In a Swiss lake: pike (Esox lucius) hunt pearlfish (Rutilus meidingeri). These eat great diving beetle larvae (Dytiscus marginalis), which in turn eat various small crustaceans that feed on algae. Indicate for each of the following species whether it has, directly or indirectly, a positive effect on the abundance of small crustaceans (true) or not (false).

A. Great diving beetle larvae (Dytiscus marginalis)

B. Pearlfish (Rutilus meidingeri)

C. Pike (Esox lucius)

D. Algae

The figure shows temperature–performance curves of four species (A, B, C, D). The dotted line shows the current temperature in the shared habitat. Which of the four species will lose the most productivity under a general rise in temperature?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-58-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Leistung = performance; Temperatur = temperature.

Air quality can be measured and assessed with bioindicators (indicator species) and physicochemical methods. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. To quantify results from studies with bioindicators, these must be converted into comparable indices.

B. The two methods have different detection limits.

C. Pollutants measured physicochemically are irrelevant to living organisms.

D. Bioindicators allow conclusions to be drawn about earlier exposure to pollutants.

Which curve best corresponds to bacterial growth when medium is added continuously?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2018-1-60-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Populationsgrösse = population size; Generationen = generations.

To which group of molecules does the compound in the figure belong?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2019-1-1-fig1.png

A. Carbohydrates

B. Nucleic acids

C. Proteins

D. Lipids

Indicate for each of the following enzymes whether it is involved in DNA replication (true) or not (false).

A. α-Amylase

B. DNA polymerase

C. Helicase

D. Lysozyme

The transcription factor E2F activates, when required, the expression of genes that drive the cell cycle. The protein Rb (retinoblastoma protein) can bind to E2F and thereby inhibit it. The Rb protein is mutated in certain tumours of the retina of the eye. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Rb reduces the expression of the genes controlled by E2F.

B. Overexpression of rb promotes cell division.

C. A defect of Rb can lead to excessive cell growth.

D. A mutation in the e2F gene that results in E2F no longer being able to bind to Rb prevents cell division.

The figure shows schematically the building blocks of DNA and RNA. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2019-1-4-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Adenin = adenine; Guanin = guanine; Thymin (DNA) = thymine (DNA); Uracil (RNA) = uracil (RNA); Cytosin = cytosine; Purine = purines; Pyrimidine = pyrimidines; Stickstoffbase = nitrogenous base; Pentose = pentose; Phosphat = phosphate; Deoxyribose (DNA) = deoxyribose (DNA); Ribose (RNA) = ribose (RNA).

A. The sugar building block of RNA has one OH group fewer than that of DNA.

B. The pentoses and the phosphate groups form the backbone of nucleic acids.

C. Adenine can form a base pair both with thymine and with uracil.

D. The phosphate groups electrostatically attract negatively charged ions (anions).

The inner mitochondrial membrane is impermeable to most ions. However, there are pumps which selectively transport H⁺ from the matrix (interior of the mitochondrion) into the space between the inner and the outer mitochondrial membrane. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. If the inner membrane were permeable to H⁺ ions, the H⁺ concentration in the matrix would be higher than in the intermembrane space.

The Michaelis–Menten model describes the catalysis of enzymatic reactions. It is based on the following concept:

$$\mathrm{E} + \mathrm{S} \underset{k_{off}}{\overset{k_{on}}{\rightleftharpoons}} [\mathrm{ES}] \xrightarrow{k_{cat}} \mathrm{P} + \mathrm{E}$$

From this model, the following function can be described:

$$v_0 = \frac{v_{max} \cdot [S]}{K_m + [S]}$$

$v_0$: initial rate

$v_{max}$: maximum reaction rate

$K_m$: Michaelis constant ([S] at which half the maximum rate is reached.)
